main_text.p: fidera in classes redigerent sibi animo finxisse. quàm Astronomos, pateat) duas Assheerias [?], (hanc scil. quæ in Cane majore, & alteram quæ in Canicula (الشعرى) Assheera L'Gomaisa & AlGomus dictam) sorores fuisse Sohaili, qui cùm in uxorem ductæ (الجوزا) Al'Janza, dorsum fregisset & Austrum versus fugerit, sequente eam ultra viam lacteam sorore Al'obur, dum interim AlGomaisa loco suo manens fleverit i.e. usque ad oculorum lippitudinem. hæc videre est apud Alsufium, Authorem libri [?] & ejus Epitomatorem in [?] nec non Alfaubar: & AlFirauzabad. & Authorem libri unde ratio nominis (الغميصا) peti potest, scil. quod sit AlGomaisa (اقل نورا من العبور) i.e. minùs lucida quàm AlObur. appellatur aliàs Sirius, (الشعرى الشامية) Assheera Yamanensis, quoniam (مغيبها في شق اليمن) i.e. Occasus ejus est ad plagam Yamanensem; nec non (كلب الجبار) i.e. Canis Gigantis, scil. (لاذها تتبع الجوزا ابدا) quòd semper sequatur AlJanza, i.e. Orionem. Inter hujus stellæ cultores celebris fuit (ابو كبشة) Abu Cabshah quidam, quem nonnulli eundem cum Wahebo, Mohammedis avo, esse volunt: alii Chozaensem, qui Koraishitis ut simulachris neglectis sacros ei honores deferrent, suadere conatus est; quare & postea Mohammedem, cùm eosdem à simulachrorum cultu abducere vellet, filium Abi Cabshæ nominârunt. referentibus Ebnol Aibir, AlFirauzabadio, AlKodaio, & Al-Bidawio in Comm. suo in Alc. cap. (...) ad verba ista (وهو رب الشعرى) i.e. Et ille [Deus scil.] Dominus est Syrii.الغموص Al'aub.E contra ea quæ in Canicula الشعرى الشامية Assheera Syra, aliâs tamen & Gemini (الجوزا) dicuntur Gemin. lib. (التبيان)

page.notes: Arabic words in the text are transcribed as far as legible; the Arabic in the text after "libri" and "in" (the title of the work) and the Arabic cross-reference in the margin "الغموص" are doubtful. The inline Arabic in the text after "Abu Cabshah", "Assheerias" (the spelling of the first letters) and the Arabic in the phrase "Alc. cap." (...) are uncertain. The margin note block at the left, with "التبيان", is set in a different size and placed beside the text lines; its Arabic is read as printed. The faint "Gc" at the bottom right edge is a digitiser mark and is omitted. Fine image detail at the edges is not printed text.
